item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
781
ABPZ20 KNHC 051116
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Sep 5 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane Karina, located about 800 hundred
miles east of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Marie, located
several hundred miles west of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to develop well offshore of
southwestern Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible
thereafter, and a tropical depression could form during the second
half of the week while the system moves generally west-northwestward
at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 051442
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026
 
...MARIE EXPECTED TO WEAKEN DURING THE NEXT FEW DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...21.8N 120.4W
ABOUT 675 MI...1085 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 21.8 North, longitude 120.4 West. Marie is moving
toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A similar motion is 
expected today. A slight decrease in forward speed with a brief 
turn toward the west-northwest is possible on Sunday. Marie 
is then expected to resume a northwestward heading at a faster 
forward speed.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher
gusts. Steady weakening is forecast through early next week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles
(335 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster D. Zelinsky

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 18
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 051442
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  18
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Sat Sep 05 2026
 
Marie's appearance has changed little since the last advisory. 
Recent IR satellite imagery indicates the hurricane continues 
to have a ragged banding eye with a dry air wrapping around the 
north of its center. The initial intensity remains 80 kt for this 
advisory, based on the latest TAFB Dvorak estimate of 4.5/77 kt and 
the UW-CIMSS objective estimates including SATCON, DPRINT, and 
DMINT which were all around 80 kt as of 1200 UTC.

Only very slight changes were made to the NHC forecast for Marie to 
show a slightly faster storm motion during the next couple of days. 
Otherwise, the forecast is very similar to the previous advisory and 
remains heavily based on the HCCA consensus. The hurricane is 
forecast to move northwestward for the next day or two, generally 
along the western periphery of a ridge centered over the southern 
United States. Slow weakening is expected during this period as the 
cyclone encounters gradually drier air (SHIPS diagnostics indicate 
environmental RH below 60 percent) and SSTs of 25-27 deg C. 

A temporary west-northwestward bend will be possible next week as 
Marie becomes weaker and shallower, but the cyclone should 
ultimately accelerate northwestward or north-northwestward by 
late Tuesday in response to a deep-layer trough that models 
indicate will build to its west. The forecast uncertainty increases 
during this period, but the model spread has decreased since 
yesterday so confidence in the forecast is growing. Simulated 
satellite imagery indicates Marie will lose its remaining deep 
convection and become a remnant low near or just after 96 h.
